content: Strong inducers of the hepatic enzyme CYP3A4 can significantly reduce the plasma concentrations of midostaurin, potentially leading to a decrease in its therapeutic efficacy. Close monitoring of the patient is advised. Nafcillin can lower the levels or diminish the effects of mifepristone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism in the liver and intestines. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. The coadministration of CYP3A4 inducers with mifepristone has not been extensively studied, and the manufacturer does not recommend this combination. Alternative therapies should be considered. Minocycline can antagonize the pharmacodynamic effects of nafcillin, reducing its efficacy. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Bacteriostatic antibiotics, such as tetracyclines, may interfere with the bactericidal activity of penicillins, including nafcillin. Avoid this combination or consider alternative therapies. Nafcillin and mycophenolate can mutually increase each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Close monitoring is required if coadministration is necessary. Nafcillin can reduce the levels or effects of naldemedine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Physiologically-based pharmacokinetic modeling suggests that moderate CYP3A4 inducers can decrease naldemedine exposure. The clinical significance of this reduced exposure is currently unknown. Nafcillin can lower the levels or effects of naloxegol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. The use of naloxegol with strong CYP3A4 inducers is not recommended. Nafcillin can reduce the levels or effects of nefazodone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Nafcillin can lower the levels or effects of nelfinavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Nafcillin can reduce the levels or effects of neratinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of neratinib with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers. Nafcillin can lower the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Netupitant is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4, so its use should be avoided in patients on chronic strong CYP3A4 inducers. Nafcillin can reduce the levels or effects of nevirapine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Nafcillin can lower the levels or effects of nicardipine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Nafcillin can reduce the levels or effects of nifedipine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Nafcillin can lower the levels or effects of nilotinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Nafcillin can reduce the levels or effects of nimodipine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Nafcillin can lower the levels or effects of nirogacestat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Nafcillin can reduce the levels or effects of nisoldipine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Nafcillin can lower the levels or effects of nitrendipine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Nafcillin can reduce the effects of nivolumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. Nafcillin can lower the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Nonhormonal contraceptives are advised during therapy. Nafcillin can reduce the levels or effects of norgestrel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Moderate CYP3A4 inducers may decrease progestin concentrations, so additional barrier methods should be considered. Nafcillin can lower the levels or effects of olaparib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inducers cannot be avoided, be aware of the potential for reduced efficacy of olaparib. Nafcillin can reduce the levels or effects of oliceridine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. If coadministration with a CYP3A4 inducer is necessary, consider increasing the oliceridine dose until stable drug effects are achieved. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal. If the inducer is discontinued, consider reducing the oliceridine dosage and monitor for signs of respiratory depression. Nafcillin can lower the levels or effects of olutasidenib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers decrease olutasidenib plasma concentrations and efficacy. Omadacycline can antagonize the pharmacodynamic effects of nafcillin, reducing its efficacy. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Tetracyclines may interfere with the bactericidal action of penicillins. Monitor for decreased therapeutic effects of penicillins if used concomitantly with a tetracycline. Nafcillin can reduce the levels or effects of omaveloxolone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Nafcillin can lower the levels or effects of ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Strong CYP3A4 inducers may reduce paritaprevir and ritonavir levels, leading to decreased efficacy of Viekira Pak. Nafcillin can reduce the levels or effects of ondansetron by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Nafcillin can lower the levels or effects of osilodrostat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Adjust the dose of osilodrostat if necessary during coadministration or discontinuation with strong CYP3A4 inducers. Nafcillin can reduce the levels or effects of osimertinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Avoid concomitant use of osimertinib with strong CYP3A4 inducers. Nafcillin can lower the levels of oxycodone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Nafcillin can reduce the levels or effects of paclitaxel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Nafcillin can lower the levels or effects of paclitaxel protein-bound by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Nafcillin can reduce the levels or effects of pacritinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Nafcillin can lower the levels or effects of palbociclib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Nafcillin can reduce the levels or effects of palovarotene by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Nafcillin can lower the levels of panobinostat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Strong CYP3A4 inducers can reduce panobinostat levels by approximately 70%, leading to treatment failure. Nafcillin can reduce the levels or effects of pazopanib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Nafcillin can lower the effects of pembrolizumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. Nafcillin can reduce the levels or effects of pemigatinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Nafcillin can lower the effects of penpulimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. Nafcillin can reduce the levels or effects of perampanel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Nafcillin can lower the levels or effects of pexidartinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Nafcillin can reduce the levels or effects of pimavanserin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Avoid coadministration if possible. Monitor for reduced pimavanserin efficacy. An increase in pimavanserin dosage may be needed. Nafcillin can lower the levels or effects of pimozide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Nafcillin can reduce the levels or effects of pirtobrutinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, increase the pirtobrutinib dose as recommended and monitor closely. Nafcillin can lower the levels or effects of pitolisant by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Pitolisant exposure is decreased by 50% when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inducers. If the strong CYP3A4 inducer is discontinued, reduce the pitolisant dosage by half. Nafcillin can reduce the levels or effects of polatuzumab vedotin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Polatuzumab undergoes catabolism to small peptides, amino acids, monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE), and unconjugated MMAE-related catabolites. MMAE is a CYP3A4 substrate. Coadministration with a strong CYP3A4 inducer may decrease unconjugated MMAE exposure. Nafcillin can lower the levels of pomalidomide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Nafcillin can reduce the levels or effects of ponatinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Avoid unless the coadministration outweighs the possible risk of ponatinib underexposure; monitor for signs of reduced efficacy. Nafcillin can lower the levels or effects of pralsetinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, double the current pralsetinib dose starting on Day 7 of coadministration with a strong CYP3A4 inducer. After the inducer has been discontinued for at least 14 days, resume the previous pralsetinib dose. Nafcillin can reduce the levels or effects of praziquantel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Nafcillin can lower the levels or effects of pretomanid by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Pretomanid is a CYP3A4 substrate. Avoid coadministration of strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers. Nafcillin can reduce the levels or effects of primaquine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Probenecid can increase the levels or effects of nafcillin by decreasing renal clearance. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Close monitoring is required if coadministration is necessary. Nafcillin can lower the levels or effects of progesterone intravaginal gel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Nafcillin can reduce the levels or effects of micronized progesterone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Nafcillin can lower the levels or effects of natural progesterone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Nafcillin can reduce the levels or effects of quetiapine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Nafcillin can lower the levels or effects of quinidine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Nafcillin can reduce the levels or effects of quinine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Nafcillin can lower the levels or effects of quizartinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Nafcillin can reduce the levels or effects of rabeprazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Nafcillin can lower the levels or effects of ranolazine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Nafcillin can reduce the levels or effects of regorafenib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Strong CYP3A4 inducers decrease regorafenib levels and increase exposure to the active metabolite M-5. Nafcillin can lower the levels or effects of repaglinide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Nafcillin can reduce the levels or effects of repotrectinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Nafcillin can lower the effects of retifanlimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. Nafcillin can reduce the levels or effects of ribociclib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely.
